title: Universal degree-zero structure-sheaf pushforward for reduced connected proper flat spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to Y$ a proper flat finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed; flatness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts, and finite presentation also includes quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. A geometric fibre is a base change to the spectrum of an algebraically closed field; integral means nonempty, reduced and irreducible. Suppose every geometric fibre is reduced and connected, where connected includes nonemptiness. Then the canonical map $\mathcal O_Y\to f_*\mathcal O_X$ on the small etale sites is an isomorphism, and for every algebraic space $T\to Y$ the canonical map $\mathcal O_T\to(f_T)_*\mathcal O_{X\times_YT}$ is an isomorphism. Direct image and tensor pullback are the canonical functors on small etale module sheaves [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors].

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary field-valued morphism $u:\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], $X_u=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}k$ is an algebraic space. The base-change assertion of [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality] makes $X_u\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ proper (also flat and finitely presented). Thus the properness hypothesis of the field calculation applies to the actual field fibre, without assuming it is a scheme.

For any algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$, the iterated fibre $(X_u)_\Omega$ is $X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$: both represent a point of $X$ and a point of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ with equal image in $Y$. The composite $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y$ is a geometric point, so the hypothesis on $f$ makes this space reduced, nonempty and connected. Apply [lem-sfb-space-proper-field-global-functions] to $X_u/k$. It proves that the canonical map $k\to\Gamma(X_u,\mathcal O_{X_u})$ is an isomorphism. No conversion from geometric fibres to a scheme-only definition of geometric connectedness is used.

The preceding field-valued morphism was arbitrary, so the field-map hypothesis of [lem-sfb-space-proper-flat-h0-criterion] holds for every $u$. Its remaining proper, flat and finite-presentation hypotheses are exactly those on $f$. The criterion gives the canonical isomorphism $\mathcal O_Y\to f_*\mathcal O_X$ together with the same canonical isomorphism after every algebraic-space base change $T\to Y$. This proves both assertions, including parameters $T$ which are not schemes.
